newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal inflation seen near 2.0 pct end year.
newsitem.headline: Portugal inflation seen near 2.0 pct end year.

text.p: Portugal could end the year with its inflation rate close to two percent, a senior Bank of Portugal official was quoted as saying on Thursday.

Abel Mateus, a central bank board member, told Diario Economico in an interview that he did not see inflation posing any problem for Portugal's eventual qualification for the European Union's planned single currency.
"Finally, we have achieved this year what is called price stability," he said. Mateus did not say whether the two percent referred to the year-on-year rate or the 12-month average.
The government has set a target range for the 12-month average of 2.25-2.5 percent for December, down from its current 3.2 percent. The year-on-year rate stood at 2.5 percent in March.
Mateus said that an inflation rate of around 2.7 percent should be sufficient to meet the Maastricht Treaty criterion for entry to the single currency.
He denied that the Bank of Portugal, which has been traditionally cautious on reducing interest rates, was adopting an excessively restrictive monetary stance.
"I see no evidence that it is limiting real growth in the economy," he said.
He noted that real interest rates, after the inflation rate had been subtracted, stood at some three percent which was an historic low for Portugal and comparable with that of Germany.
Despite the success achieved in reducing inflation, he said that the Bank was still not satisfied.
"We want to achieve a rate of between zero and 2.0 percent, which represents price stability," he said.
